plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 4: Organic Compounds: Cycloalkanes and Their Stereochemistry
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a vertical bar chart of twelve blue bars on a pale blue field, showing strain energy as a function of cycloalkane ring size. The horizontal axis is labeled Ring size and ticked at every integer from 3 to 14. The same quantity is given two vertical scales: the left axis, labeled Strain energy (kJ/mol), runs from 0 to 120 in steps of 20 with horizontal gridlines, and the right axis, labeled (kcal/mol), runs from 0 to 28.7 with tick labels 4.8, 9.6, 14.3, 19.1 and 23.9. Bars stand at every ring size except 6 and 14; at those two positions a short downward arrow with the numeral 0 above it points to the baseline in place of a bar. The two tallest bars sit at the left, about 115 kJ/mol at ring size 3 and slightly above 110 at ring size 4. The height then falls abruptly to roughly 26 at 5 and 25 at 7, rises through 40 at 8 to a secondary maximum near 53 at 9, eases to 50 at 10 and 46 at 11, drops to about 10 at 12, and returns to 22 at 13. The profile is jagged rather than smooth, so the eye tracks an irregular march of strain across ring sizes rather than a trend. The chart presents the strain energies obtained by subtracting an acyclic reference heat of combustion per CH2 unit and scaling by the number of CH2 units in the ring.

interactionPlan.concept: Ring strain in cycloalkanes varies irregularly with ring size: three- and four-membered rings are enormously strained, cyclohexane is strain-free, medium rings (8–13) carry moderate transannular strain, and large rings return to zero strain.
elements: Vertical bar chart on a pale blue plot field with a white outer background
Left y-axis labeled 'Strain energy (kJ/mol)' from 0 to 120 in steps of 20
Horizontal gridlines at 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120 kJ/mol
Right y-axis labeled '(kcal/mol)' from 0 to 28.7 with tick labels 0, 4.8, 9.6, 14.3, 19.1, 23.9
X-axis labeled 'Ring size' with integer ticks 3 through 14
Twelve x-positions; ten solid medium-blue bars at ring sizes 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13
Zero-strain markers at ring sizes 6 and 14: a short downward arrow ending at the baseline with the numeral '0' above it, replacing a bar
Baseline axis line at y = 0
Readout annotation (interactive) showing selected ring size with its kJ/mol and kcal/mol values
Optional highlight band grouping the medium rings (8–13) when discussed

interactions.label: Ring size (n carbons)
interactions.teaches: Reading strain energy for one ring at a time in both kJ/mol and kcal/mol, and feeling that the value jumps up and down rather than trending smoothly as the ring grows.
That the missing bars at ring sizes 6 and 14 are not missing data but genuine zeros — cyclohexane and large rings adopt geometries with no angle, torsional, or transannular strain.

interactions.label: Strain regions
interactions.teaches: That the jagged profile organizes into four classic categories — small rings (3–4, angle strain), common rings (5–7, near strain-free), medium rings (8–13, transannular strain), and large rings (14+, strain-free).

demo_steps.title: The whole landscape
demo_steps.narration: Twelve cycloalkanes, one bar each. The profile is jagged: two towering bars on the left, a deep valley, a broad secondary hump, and zeros at 6 and 14.

demo_steps.title: Small rings: angle strain dominates
demo_steps.narration: Slide to 3 and 4. Cyclopropane carries about 115 kJ/mol and cyclobutane about 110 — bond angles forced far below 109.5° plus eclipsing interactions make these rings the most strained of all.

demo_steps.title: The collapse at cyclohexane
demo_steps.narration: Move to 5, then 6. Strain plunges to ~26 kJ/mol at cyclopentane and to exactly zero at cyclohexane — click the arrow at 6 to see that the chair conformation relieves all angle and torsional strain.

demo_steps.title: Medium rings climb back up
demo_steps.narration: From 7 onward strain rises again, peaking near 53 kJ/mol at cyclononane. These medium rings suffer transannular strain — hydrogens across the ring crowding into each other.

demo_steps.title: Large rings relax
demo_steps.narration: By 12 and 13 strain falls off, and at 14 it is zero again: large rings are floppy enough to adopt strain-free conformations like extended alkane chains.

demo_steps.title: Four regimes, one picture
demo_steps.narration: Turn on the region shading: small (3–4), common (5–7), medium (8–13), and large (14+). The irregular bar heights are really four different physical causes of strain acting in different size ranges.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Ring strain does not decrease smoothly as rings get bigger — it collapses to zero at cyclohexane, rebounds in the medium rings because of transannular crowding, and only vanishes again once the ring is large enough to behave like an open chain.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Recreate as a Chart.js vertical bar chart: pale blue (#e8f4fb) plot area, medium-blue bars (#1a75bc) with thin darker outlines, white page background, black axis text. Left axis 'Strain energy (kJ/mol)' 0–120 step 20 with light gray horizontal gridlines; right axis '(kcal/mol)' 0–28.7 with ticks 0, 4.8, 9.6, 14.3, 19.1, 23.9 (same physical scale, 1 kcal = 4.184 kJ). X-axis 'Ring size' ticks 3–14, bars at all positions except 6 and 14, where a short thin black downward arrow tipped at the baseline carries a '0' label above it. Bar silhouette must read: two very tall bars at 3 and 4, sharp drop to short bars at 5 and 7, a rising hump 8→9 peaking ~53, gentle decline 10, 11, a low bar at 12, a modest bar at 13. Selected bar (slider) turns a saturated highlight color (e.g. orange #e8730c) with a floating readout box giving 'n = X · YY kJ/mol · ZZ kcal/mol'; non-selected bars dim slightly. Clicking a zero marker at 6 or 14 thickens and reddens the arrow, pulses the '0', and dims all bars except the immediate neighbors so the contrast with adjacent strained rings stays visible. Region toggle overlays four translucent vertical bands behind the bars with small top labels: 'Small (angle strain)', 'Common', 'Medium (transannular)', 'Large'.

authoredContext:
Because the heat of combustion of a cycloalkane depends on size, we need to look at heats of combustion per CH2 unit. Subtracting a reference value derived from a strain-free acyclic alkane and then multiplying by the number of CH2 units in the ring gives the overall strain energy. The figure shows the results.

The data in the figure show that Baeyer’s theory is only partially correct. Cyclopropane and cyclobutane are indeed strained, just as predicted, but cyclopentane is more strained than predicted, and cyclohexane is strain-free. Cycloalkanes of intermediate size have only modest strain, and rings of 14 carbons or more are strain-free. Why is Baeyer’s theory wrong?

Cycloalkane strain energies, as calculated by taking the difference between cycloalkane heat of combustion per CH2 and acyclic alkane heat of combustion per CH2, and multiplying by the number of CH2 units in a ring. Small and medium rings are strained, but cyclohexane rings and very large rings are strain-free.

Bar graph shows strain energies in cycloalkanes with strain energy in kilojoules per mole and kilocalories per mol for various ring sizes from 3-14. Strain energy is highest for 3-carbon ring.

discrepancies: Bar width/spacing differs slightly: source bars are a bit wider relative to the category gaps, giving a slightly denser look than the generated chart.

Right-hand '(kcal/mol)' axis title is rendered in a smaller font and sits closer to the tick labels than in the source, where it is a clearly separated rotated title of the same weight as the left title.

Source draws x-axis tick marks at the category boundaries with a heavier axis rule; the generated axis line/ticks are lighter and the category ticks land under label centers, a minor styling deviation.

The 'Strain regions' overlay assigns 12 and 13 to the 'medium' band while the step narration describes 12–13 as relaxing toward large-ring behaviour — a small internal inconsistency not present in the source.
evaluation.notes: A near drop-in replacement for the source bar chart — correct values, dual kJ/kcal axes, pale blue plot field, blue bars and both '0' down-arrows at n=6 and n=14 — backed by a genuinely useful set of interactions (ring-size slider, strain-region shading, 6-step guided tour, click popups); only minor label sizing/placement and a small medium/large-ring classification inconsistency detract.
action_items: Increase the right-axis '(kcal/mol)' title font to match the left axis title and add a little padding so it does not crowd the tick labels.
Widen the bars slightly (raise barPercentage toward ~0.8) to match the source's bar-to-gap ratio.
Ensure the selection readout box is always positioned to avoid overlapping tall bars (e.g. flip it to the left half when a bar near the right edge is selected, or when region labels are on).
Reconcile the region band boundaries with the narration text (either label 12–13 as large or reword step 5).

feedback.rationale: No failure modes, all core dimensions score 5 with a 4.8 overall, and the remaining action items are trivial cosmetic tweaks that don't warrant another iteration.
